summary: This document updates RFC 8928 by changing the position of the C-flag in the Extended Address Registration Option and registering it with IANA. The change fixes a flaw in how the flag was originally placed.

eli5.summary: A checkbox was in the wrong place on a form. This moves it and records the new place.

questions: where is the c-flag in rfc 8928
what is the earo in 6lowpan nd
why was the c-flag moved to bit 1
subtitle: Moves the C-flag to bit 1 of the EARO flags field so it no longer overlaps the P-field.

tldr.problem: RFC 8928 put the C-flag at bit 3 of the EARO flags field without registering it with IANA, and RFC 9685 later defined the P-field in bits 2 and 3, so the two overlapped.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9927 moves the C-flag to bit 1 of the EARO flags field, redraws the EARO formats for NS and NA messages, and registers bit 1 with IANA.
tldr.outcome: The change is not backward compatible, but the RFC notes there are no known implementations or deployments of RFC 8928, so no transition plan is needed.

facts.label: New C-flag position
facts.value: Bit 1 of the EARO flags field

today: RFC 9927 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2026. It updates RFC 8928 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Overlapping Flag
sections.content:
RFC 8928 (Address-Protected Neighbor Discovery for Low-Power and Lossy Networks) defined the C-flag in the Extended Address Registration Option (EARO). It indicates that the Registration Ownership Verifier (ROVR) field holds a Crypto-ID and that the 6LoWPAN Node (6LN) may be challenged for ownership of the registered address.

RFC 8928 placed the flag at bit position 3. Later, RFC 9685 defined a P-field in bits 2 and 3 of the EARO flags field, with proper IANA registration. That overlapped the C-flag drawn in Figure 1 of RFC 8928.
sections.eli5: Two rules claimed the same spot on the same form, so one had to move.

sections.title: What Changes in RFC 8928
sections.content:
RFC 9927 repositions the C-flag to bit 1 of the EARO flags field, so no definitions overlap. It also corrects a naming slip: RFC 8928 called the option the Enhanced Address Registration Option, and this document fixes that to Extended throughout.

Its Figure 1 replaces Figure 1 of RFC 8928 for an EARO in a Neighbor Solicitation (NS), and its Figure 2 does so for a Neighbor Advertisement (NA). The two differ only in bits 16 to 23.

The C-flag stays a 1-bit flag. It is set to show that the ROVR field contains a Crypto-ID and that the 6LN MAY be challenged for ownership.
sections.eli5: The checkbox keeps its meaning but gets a new box on the form, and the old form is replaced.

sections.title: The Updated EARO Fields
sections.content:
The flags row now reads r, C, P (2 bits), I (2 bits), R and T, followed by the 8-bit TID and the 16-bit Registration Lifetime. Then comes the ROVR, which is 64, 128, 192 or 256 bits.

The P field is a 2-bit Registered Address Type Indicator (RATInd): unicast, multicast, anycast, or derived from the registered unicast prefix. Status is a 6-bit unsigned integer used only in NA(EARO) messages; it MUST be 0 in NS(EARO) unless the registration is for a prefix, in which case the F-flag is set. Reserved bits MUST be set to zero by the sender and ignored by the receiver. The option Type is 33.
sections.eli5: The form has small boxes in a row. Each one holds one fact, and the reserved boxes stay empty.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This specification introduces no new security considerations beyond those already discussed in RFC 8928 and RFC 8505.
sections.eli5: Only the spot of one checkbox moved, so there is nothing new to worry about.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content: The updates in this document are not backward compatible. However, the RFC states that there are no known implementations or deployments of RFC 8928, so it requires no transition plan.
sections.eli5: Old forms will not match the new one, but nobody was using the old form yet.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA has updated the Address Registration Option Flags registry in the ICMPv6 Parameters registry group. Bit number 1, the C-Flag, now cites RFC 9927 in addition to RFC 8928.
sections.eli5: The official list now says the checkbox lives in bit 1.
